President Bola Tinubu arrived in Lagos on Saturday after attending the All Progressives Congress presidential campaign rally in Ibadan, Oyo State. His aircraft landed at the Presidential Wing of the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Ikeja, at about 3pm, according to a statement by his Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga. Tinubu was received by Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu, Ogun State Governor Dapo Abiodun, his Chief of Staff, Femi Gbajabiamila, and former Ogun State Governor Segun Osoba. Other government officials, party leaders and supporters were also at the airport to welcome him. “While in Lagos on the short visit, President Tinubu is scheduled to attend a special prayer session organised in his honour by members of his family on Sunday, November 22,” the statement said. At the rally, he promised improved electricity supply in Oyo State and disclosed that his administration had reached an agreement with Chinese automobile manufacturer Yutong to revive the old Leyland factory in Ibadan for vehicle assembly. He also urged residents to support the APC in the 2027 elections and publicly endorsed the party’s governorship candidates in Oyo, Ogun and Lagos states, as well as its Oyo South senatorial candidate. The event was held without much fanfare following the President’s directive in honour of victims of the Bayelsa boat accident, with a minute’s silence observed for those who died.
